questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $2,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)={t}^{2}-t,\,{p}_{2}(t)={t}^{2}+t,\,q(t)=4{t}^{2}-t-1
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}$ equals $2{t}^{2}-2t.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the vector space of continuous functions over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$, and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{f}_{1}(t)=1,\,{f}_{2}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,g(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{2}(t)}$ equals $-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t)={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{⟨g(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩}{⟨{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩}\,{f}_{1}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }g(t){f}_{1}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3)\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =[-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3t]_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(2-0+3\pi )-(2-0-3\pi ) \\  & =6\pi \end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }1\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }1\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t) & =\frac{6\pi }{2\pi }\cdot 1=3.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t) \\  & =3-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $2$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the distance between $p(t)=5{t}^{2}-5$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t+1$ with respect to the inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)}{q(-1)q(-1)+q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1)}\cdot q(t) \\  & =\frac{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(5{t}^{2}-5){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t+1){|}_{t=i}}{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(t+1){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t+1){|}_{t=i}}\cdot (t+1) \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1+0\cdot 2}{0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1+2\cdot 2}\cdot (t+1) \\  & =\frac{-5}{5}\cdot (t+1) \\  & =-t-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The distance between $p(t)=5{t}^{2}-5$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t+1$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖p(t)-{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)‖ \\  & =‖5{t}^{2}-5-(-t-1)‖ \\  & =‖5{t}^{2}+t-4‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨5{t}^{2}+t-4,5{t}^{2}+t-4⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨5{t}^{2}+t-4,5{t}^{2}+t-4⟩ & ={\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(5{t}^{2}+t-4){|}_{t=i}\cdot (5{t}^{2}+t-4){|}_{t=i} \\  & =(0)\cdot (0)+(-4)\cdot (-4)+2\cdot 2 \\  & =0+16+4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{20}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the distance between $f(t)=7t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-2$ with respect to the inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}7t\cdot (t-2)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}(t-2)^{2}\,\text{d}t}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}(7{t}^{2}-14t)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}-4t+4)\,\text{d}t}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{[\frac{7}{3}{t}^{3}-7{t}^{2}]_{0}^{1}}{[\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+4t]_{0}^{1}}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{14}{3})}{(\frac{7}{3})}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =-2t+4.\end{aligned}
$$

The distance between $f(t)=7t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-2$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖f(t)-{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)‖ \\  & =‖7t-(-2t+4)‖ \\  & =‖9t-4‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨9t-4,9t-4⟩}\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨9t-4,9t-4⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9t-4)\cdot (9t-4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9t-4)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(81{t}^{2}-72t+16)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(27{t}^{3}-36{t}^{2}+16)\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{7}.$
